tbesh_html:
1) to carve, engrave
1a) (Piel) to engrave
1b) (Pual) to be engraved

strongs_1890.strongs_def: to open wide (literally or figuratively); specifically, to loosen, begin, plough, carve
strongs_1890.kjv_def: appear, break forth, draw (out), let go free, (en-) grave(-n), loose (self), (be, be set) open(-ing), put off, ungird, unstop, have vent.

occurrences.bsb: In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, on the seventeenth day of the second month, all the fountains of the great deep burst forth, and the floodgates of the heavens were opened.
occurrences.kjv: In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, in the second month, the seventeenth day of the month, the same day were all the fountains of the great deep broken up, and the windows of heaven were opened.

occurrences.bsb: After forty days Noah opened the window he had made in the ark
occurrences.kjv: And it came to pass at the end of forty days, that Noah opened the window of the ark which he had made:

occurrences.bsb: So the man came to the house, and the camels were unloaded. Straw and feed were brought to the camels, and water to wash his feet and the feet of his companions.
occurrences.kjv: And the man came into the house: and he ungirded his camels, and gave straw and provender for the camels, and water to wash his feet, and the men’s feet that were with him.

occurrences.bsb: When the LORD saw that Leah was unloved, He opened her womb; but Rachel was barren.
occurrences.kjv: And when the Lord saw that Leah was hated, he opened her womb: but Rachel was barren.

occurrences.bsb: Then God remembered Rachel. He listened to her and opened her womb,
occurrences.kjv: And God remembered Rachel, and God hearkened to her, and opened her womb.

occurrences.bsb: When the famine had spread over all the land, Joseph opened up all the storehouses and sold grain to the Egyptians; for the famine was severe in the land of Egypt.
occurrences.kjv: And the famine was over all the face of the earth: And Joseph opened all the storehouses, and sold unto the Egyptians; and the famine waxed sore in the land of Egypt.

occurrences.bsb: At the place where they lodged for the night, one of them opened his sack to get feed for his donkey, and he saw his silver in the mouth of the sack.
occurrences.kjv: And as one of them opened his sack to give his ass provender in the inn, he espied his money; for, behold, it was in his sack’s mouth.

occurrences.bsb: But when we came to the place we lodged for the night, we opened our sacks and, behold, each of us found his silver in the mouth of his sack! It was the full amount of our silver, and we have brought it back with us.
occurrences.kjv: And it came to pass, when we came to the inn, that we opened our sacks, and, behold, every man’s money was in the mouth of his sack, our money in full weight: and we have brought it again in our hand.

occurrences.bsb: So each one quickly lowered his sack to the ground and opened it.
occurrences.kjv: Then they speedily took down every man his sack to the ground, and opened every man his sack.

occurrences.bsb: When she opened it, she saw the child, and behold, the little boy was crying. So she had compassion on him and said, “This is one of the Hebrew children.”
occurrences.kjv: And when she had opened it, she saw the child: and, behold, the babe wept. And she had compassion on him, and said, This is one of the Hebrews’ children.

occurrences.bsb: If a man opens or digs a pit and fails to cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls into it,
occurrences.kjv: And if a man shall open a pit, or if a man shall dig a pit, and not cover it, and an ox or an ass fall therein;

occurrences.bsb: Take two onyx stones and engrave on them the names of the sons of Israel:
occurrences.kjv: And thou shalt take two onyx stones, and grave on them the names of the children of Israel:

occurrences.bsb: Engrave the names of the sons of Israel on the two stones the way a gem cutter engraves a seal. Then mount the stones in gold filigree settings.
occurrences.kjv: With the work of an engraver in stone, like the engravings of a signet, shalt thou engrave the two stones with the names of the children of Israel: thou shalt make them to be set in ouches of gold.

occurrences.bsb: You are to make a plate of pure gold and engrave on it as on a seal: HOLY TO THE LORD.
occurrences.kjv: And thou shalt make a plate of pure gold, and grave upon it, like the engravings of a signet, HOLINESS TO THE LORD.

occurrences.bsb: They mounted the onyx stones in gold filigree settings, engraved like a seal with the names of the sons of Israel.
occurrences.kjv: And they wrought onyx stones inclosed in ouches of gold, graven, as signets are graven, with the names of the children of Israel.

occurrences.bsb: and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and their households—all Korah’s men and all their possessions.
occurrences.kjv: And the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up, and their houses, and all the men that appertained unto Korah, and all their goods.

occurrences.bsb: and any open container without a lid fastened on it is unclean.
occurrences.kjv: And every open vessel, which hath no covering bound upon it, is unclean.

occurrences.bsb: Then the LORD opened the donkey’s mouth, and she said to Balaam, “What have I done to you that you have beaten me these three times?”
occurrences.kjv: And the Lord opened the mouth of the ass, and she said unto Balaam, What have I done unto thee, that thou hast smitten me these three times?

occurrences.bsb: And the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them along with Korah, whose followers died when the fire consumed 250 men. They serve as a warning sign.
occurrences.kjv: And the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up together with Korah, when that company died, what time the fire devoured two hundred and fifty men: and they became a sign.

occurrences.bsb: Instead, you are to open your hand to him and freely loan him whatever he needs.
occurrences.kjv: But thou shalt open thine hand wide unto him, and shalt surely lend him sufficient for his need, in that which he wanteth.

occurrences.bsb: For there will never cease to be poor in the land; that is why I am commanding you to open wide your hand to your brother and to the poor and needy in your land.
occurrences.kjv: For the poor shall never cease out of the land: therefore I command thee, saying, Thou shalt open thine hand wide unto thy brother, to thy poor, and to thy needy, in thy land.

occurrences.bsb: If they accept your offer of peace and open their gates, all the people there will become forced laborers to serve you.
occurrences.kjv: And it shall be, if it make thee answer of peace, and open unto thee, then it shall be, that all the people that is found therein shall be tributaries unto thee, and they shall serve thee.

occurrences.bsb: The LORD will open the heavens, His abundant storehouse, to send rain on your land in season and to bless all the work of your hands. You will lend to many nations, but borrow from none.
occurrences.kjv: The Lord shall open unto thee his good treasure, the heaven to give the rain unto thy land in his season, and to bless all the work of thine hand: and thou shalt lend unto many nations, and thou shalt not borrow.

occurrences.bsb: Not a man was left in Ai or Bethel who did not go out after Israel, leaving the city wide open while they pursued Israel.
occurrences.kjv: And there was not a man left in Ai or Beth–el, that went not out after Israel: and they left the city open, and pursued after Israel.

occurrences.bsb: Then Joshua said, “Open the mouth of the cave and bring those five kings out to me.”
occurrences.kjv: Then said Joshua, Open the mouth of the cave, and bring out those five kings unto me out of the cave.

occurrences.bsb: So they waited until they became worried and saw that he had still not opened the doors of the upper room. Then they took the key and opened the doors—and there was their lord lying dead on the floor.
occurrences.kjv: And they tarried till they were ashamed: and, behold, he opened not the doors of the parlour; therefore they took a key, and opened them: and, behold, their lord was fallen down dead on the earth.

occurrences.bsb: Sisera said to her, “Please give me a little water to drink, for I am thirsty.” So she opened a container of milk, gave him a drink, and covered him again.
occurrences.kjv: And he said unto her, Give me, I pray thee, a little water to drink; for I am thirsty. And she opened a bottle of milk, and gave him drink, and covered him.

occurrences.bsb: In the morning, when her master got up and opened the doors of the house to go out on his journey, there was his concubine, collapsed in the doorway of the house, with her hands on the threshold.
occurrences.kjv: And her lord rose up in the morning, and opened the doors of the house, and went out to go his way: and, behold, the woman his concubine was fallen down at the door of the house, and her hands were upon the threshold.

occurrences.bsb: Samuel lay down until the morning; then he opened the doors of the house of the LORD. He was afraid to tell Eli the vision,
occurrences.kjv: And Samuel lay until the morning, and opened the doors of the house of the Lord. And Samuel feared to shew Eli the vision.

occurrences.bsb: He engraved cherubim, lions, and palm trees on the surfaces of the supports and panels, wherever each had space, with wreaths all around.
occurrences.kjv: For on the plates of the ledges thereof, and on the borders thereof, he graved cherubims, lions, and palm trees, according to the proportion of every one, and additions round about.

occurrences.bsb: May Your eyes be open toward this temple night and day, toward the place of which You said, ‘My Name shall be there,’ so that You may hear the prayer that Your servant prays toward this place.
occurrences.kjv: That thine eyes may be open toward this house night and day, even toward the place of which thou hast said, My name shall be there: that thou mayest hearken unto the prayer which thy servant shall make toward this place.

occurrences.bsb: May Your eyes be open to the pleas of Your servant and of Your people Israel, and may You listen to them whenever they call to You.
occurrences.kjv: That thine eyes may be open unto the supplication of thy servant, and unto the supplication of thy people Israel, to hearken unto them in all that they call for unto thee.

occurrences.bsb: And the king of Israel replied, “Tell him: ‘The one putting on his armor should not boast like one taking it off.’”
occurrences.kjv: And the king of Israel answered and said, Tell him, Let not him that girdeth on his harness boast himself as he that putteth it off.

occurrences.bsb: Then take the flask of oil, pour it on his head, and declare, ‘This is what the LORD says: I anoint you king over Israel.’ Then open the door and run. Do not delay!”
occurrences.kjv: Then take the box of oil, and pour it on his head, and say, Thus saith the Lord, I have anointed thee king over Israel. Then open the door, and flee, and tarry not.

occurrences.bsb: And on the plot of ground at Jezreel the dogs will devour Jezebel, and there will be no one to bury her.’” Then the young prophet opened the door and ran.
occurrences.kjv: And the dogs shall eat Jezebel in the portion of Jezreel, and there shall be none to bury her. And he opened the door, and fled.

occurrences.bsb: “Open the east window,” said Elisha. So he opened it and Elisha said, “Shoot!” So he shot. And Elisha declared: “This is the LORD’s arrow of victory, the arrow of victory over Aram, for you shall strike the Arameans in Aphek until you have put an end to them.”
occurrences.kjv: And he said, Open the window eastward. And he opened it. Then Elisha said, Shoot. And he shot. And he said, The arrow of the Lord’s deliverance, and the arrow of deliverance from Syria: for thou shalt smite the Syrians in Aphek, till thou have consumed them.

occurrences.bsb: At that time Menahem, starting from Tirzah, attacked Tiphsah and everyone in its vicinity, because they would not open their gates. So he attacked Tiphsah and ripped open all the pregnant women.
occurrences.kjv: Then Menahem smote Tiphsah, and all that were therein, and the coasts thereof from Tirzah: because they opened not to him, therefore he smote it; and all the women therein that were with child he ripped up.

occurrences.bsb: Send me, therefore, a craftsman skilled in engraving to work with gold and silver, with bronze and iron, and with purple, crimson, and blue yarn. He will work with my craftsmen in Judah and Jerusalem, whom my father David provided.
occurrences.kjv: Send me now therefore a man cunning to work in gold, and in silver, and in brass, and in iron, and in purple, and crimson, and blue, and that can skill to grave with the cunning men that are with me in Judah and in Jerusalem, whom David my father did provide.

occurrences.bsb: He is the son of a woman from the daughters of Dan, and his father is a man of Tyre. He is skilled in work with gold and silver, bronze and iron, stone and wood, purple, blue, and crimson yarn, and fine linen. He is experienced in every kind of engraving and can execute any design that is given him. He will work with your craftsmen and with those of my lord, your father David.
occurrences.kjv: The son of a woman of the daughters of Dan, and his father was a man of Tyre, skilful to work in gold, and in silver, in brass, in iron, in stone, and in timber, in purple, in blue, and in fine linen, and in crimson; also to grave any manner of graving, and to find out every device which shall be put to him, with thy cunning men, and with the cunning men of my lord David thy father.

occurrences.bsb: He overlaid its beams, thresholds, walls, and doors with gold, and he carved cherubim on the walls.
occurrences.kjv: He overlaid also the house, the beams, the posts, and the walls thereof, and the doors thereof, with gold; and graved cherubims on the walls.

occurrences.bsb: May Your eyes be open toward this temple day and night, toward the place where You said You would put Your Name, so that You may hear the prayer that Your servant prays toward this place.
occurrences.kjv: That thine eyes may be open upon this house day and night, upon the place whereof thou hast said that thou wouldest put thy name there; to hearken unto the prayer which thy servant prayeth toward this place.

occurrences.bsb: Now, my God, may Your eyes be open and Your ears attentive to the prayer offered in this place.
occurrences.kjv: Now, my God, let, I beseech thee, thine eyes be open, and let thine ears be attent unto the prayer that is made in this place.

occurrences.bsb: Now My eyes will be open and My ears attentive to the prayers offered in this place.
occurrences.kjv: Now mine eyes shall be open, and mine ears attent unto the prayer that is made in this place.

occurrences.bsb: In the first month of the first year of his reign, Hezekiah opened and repaired the doors of the house of the LORD.
occurrences.kjv: He in the first year of his reign, in the first month, opened the doors of the house of the Lord, and repaired them.

occurrences.bsb: let Your eyes be open and Your ears attentive to hear the prayer that I, Your servant, now pray before You day and night for Your servants, the Israelites. I confess the sins that we Israelites have committed against You. Both I and my father’s house have sinned.
occurrences.kjv: Let thine ear now be attentive, and thine eyes open, that thou mayest hear the prayer of thy servant, which I pray before thee now, day and night, for the children of Israel thy servants, and confess the sins of the children of Israel, which we have sinned against thee: both I and my father’s house have sinned.

occurrences.bsb: The fifth time, Sanballat sent me this same message by his young servant, who had in his hand an unsealed letter
occurrences.kjv: Then sent Sanballat his servant unto me in like manner the fifth time with an open letter in his hand;

occurrences.bsb: And I told them, “Do not open the gates of Jerusalem until the sun is hot. While the guards are on duty, keep the doors shut and securely fastened. And appoint the residents of Jerusalem as guards, some at their posts and some at their own homes.”
occurrences.kjv: And I said unto them, Let not the gates of Jerusalem be opened until the sun be hot; and while they stand by, let them shut the doors, and bar them: and appoint watches of the inhabitants of Jerusalem, every one in his watch, and every one to be over against his house.

occurrences.bsb: Ezra opened the book in full view of all the people, since he was standing above them all, and as he opened it, all the people stood up.
occurrences.kjv: And Ezra opened the book in the sight of all the people; (for he was above all the people;) and when he opened it, all the people stood up:

occurrences.bsb: When the evening shadows began to fall on the gates of Jerusalem, just before the Sabbath, I ordered that the gates be shut and not opened until after the Sabbath. I posted some of my servants at the gates so that no load could enter on the Sabbath day.
occurrences.kjv: And it came to pass, that when the gates of Jerusalem began to be dark before the sabbath, I commanded that the gates should be shut, and charged that they should not be opened till after the sabbath: and some of my servants set I at the gates, that there should no burden be brought in on the sabbath day.

occurrences.bsb: After this, Job opened his mouth and cursed the day of his birth.
occurrences.kjv: After this opened Job his mouth, and cursed his day.

occurrences.bsb: But if only God would speak and open His lips against you,
occurrences.kjv: But oh that God would speak, and open his lips against thee;

occurrences.bsb: What He tears down cannot be rebuilt; the man He imprisons cannot be released.
occurrences.kjv: Behold, he breaketh down, and it cannot be built again: he shutteth up a man, and there can be no opening.

occurrences.bsb: He loosens the bonds placed by kings and fastens a belt around their waists.
occurrences.kjv: He looseth the bond of kings, and girdeth their loins with a girdle.

occurrences.bsb: My roots will spread out to the waters, and the dew will rest nightly on my branches.
occurrences.kjv: My root was spread out by the waters, and the dew lay all night upon my branch.

occurrences.bsb: Because God has unstrung my bow and afflicted me, they have cast off restraint in my presence.
occurrences.kjv: Because he hath loosed my cord, and afflicted me, they have also let loose the bridle before me.

occurrences.bsb: but no stranger had to lodge on the street, for my door has been open to the traveler—
occurrences.kjv: The stranger did not lodge in the street: but I opened my doors to the traveller.

occurrences.bsb: Behold, my belly is like unvented wine; it is about to burst like a new wineskin.
occurrences.kjv: Behold, my belly is as wine which hath no vent; it is ready to burst like new bottles.

occurrences.bsb: I must speak and find relief; I must open my lips and respond.
occurrences.kjv: I will speak, that I may be refreshed: I will open my lips and answer.

occurrences.bsb: Behold, I will open my mouth; my address is on the tip of my tongue.
occurrences.kjv: Behold, now I have opened my mouth, my tongue hath spoken in my mouth.

occurrences.bsb: Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades or loosen the belt of Orion?
occurrences.kjv: Canst thou bind the sweet influences of Pleiades, or loose the bands of Orion?

occurrences.bsb: Who set the wild donkey free? Who released the swift donkey from the harness?
occurrences.kjv: Who hath sent out the wild ass free? or who hath loosed the bands of the wild ass?

occurrences.bsb: Who can open his jaws, ringed by his fearsome teeth?
occurrences.kjv: Who can open the doors of his face? his teeth are terrible round about.

occurrences.bsb: For not a word they speak can be trusted; destruction lies within them. Their throats are open graves; their tongues practice deceit.
occurrences.kjv: For there is no faithfulness in their mouth; their inward part is very wickedness; their throat is an open sepulchre; they flatter with their tongue.

occurrences.bsb: You turned my mourning into dancing; You peeled off my sackcloth and clothed me with joy,
occurrences.kjv: Thou hast turned for me my mourning into dancing: thou hast put off my sackcloth, and girded me with gladness;

occurrences.bsb: The wicked have drawn the sword and bent the bow to bring down the poor and needy, to slay those whose ways are upright.
occurrences.kjv: The wicked have drawn out the sword, and have bent their bow, to cast down the poor and needy, and to slay such as be of upright conversation.

occurrences.bsb: But like a deaf man, I do not hear; and like a mute man, I do not open my mouth.
occurrences.kjv: But I, as a deaf man, heard not; and I was as a dumb man that openeth not his mouth.

occurrences.bsb: I have become mute; I do not open my mouth because of what You have done.
occurrences.kjv: I was dumb, I opened not my mouth; because thou didst it.

occurrences.bsb: I will incline my ear to a proverb; I will express my riddle with the harp:
occurrences.kjv: I will incline mine ear to a parable: I will open my dark saying upon the harp.

occurrences.bsb: O Lord, open my lips, and my mouth will declare Your praise.
occurrences.kjv: O Lord, open thou my lips; and my mouth shall shew forth thy praise.

occurrences.bsb: I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden from the beginning,
occurrences.kjv: I will open my mouth in a parable: I will utter dark sayings of old:

occurrences.bsb: Yet He commanded the clouds above and opened the doors of the heavens.
occurrences.kjv: Though he had commanded the clouds from above, and opened the doors of heaven,

occurrences.bsb: to hear a prisoner’s groaning, to release those condemned to death,
occurrences.kjv: To hear the groaning of the prisoner; to loose those that are appointed to death;

occurrences.bsb: When You give it to them, they gather it up; when You open Your hand, they are satisfied with good things.
occurrences.kjv: That thou givest them they gather: thou openest thine hand, they are filled with good.

occurrences.bsb: The king sent and released him; the ruler of peoples set him free.
occurrences.kjv: The king sent and loosed him; even the ruler of the people, and let him go free.

occurrences.bsb: He opened a rock, and water gushed out; it flowed like a river in the desert.
occurrences.kjv: He opened the rock, and the waters gushed out; they ran in the dry places like a river.

occurrences.bsb: The earth opened up and swallowed Dathan; it covered the assembly of Abiram.
occurrences.kjv: The earth opened and swallowed up Dathan, and covered the company of Abiram.

occurrences.bsb: For wicked and deceitful mouths open against me; they speak against me with lying tongues.
occurrences.kjv: For the mouth of the wicked and the mouth of the deceitful are opened against me: they have spoken against me with a lying tongue.

occurrences.bsb: Truly, O LORD, I am Your servant; I am Your servant, the son of Your maidservant; You have broken my bonds.
occurrences.kjv: O Lord, truly I am thy servant; I am thy servant, and the son of thine handmaid: thou hast loosed my bonds.

occurrences.bsb: Open to me the gates of righteousness, that I may enter and give thanks to the LORD.
occurrences.kjv: Open to me the gates of righteousness: I will go into them, and I will praise the Lord:

occurrences.bsb: You open Your hand and satisfy the desire of every living thing.
occurrences.kjv: Thou openest thine hand, and satisfiest the desire of every living thing.

occurrences.bsb: Wisdom is too high for a fool; he does not open his mouth in the meeting place.
occurrences.kjv: Wisdom is too high for a fool: he openeth not his mouth in the gate.

occurrences.bsb: Open your mouth for those with no voice, for the cause of all the dispossessed.
occurrences.kjv: Open thy mouth for the dumb in the cause of all such as are appointed to destruction.

occurrences.bsb: Open your mouth, judge righteously, and defend the cause of the poor and needy.
occurrences.kjv: Open thy mouth, judge righteously, and plead the cause of the poor and needy.

occurrences.bsb: She opens her mouth with wisdom, and faithful instruction is on her tongue.
occurrences.kjv: She openeth her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue is the law of kindness.

occurrences.bsb: I sleep, but my heart is awake. A sound! My beloved is knocking: “Open to me, my sister, my darling, my dove, my flawless one. My head is drenched with dew, my hair with the dampness of the night.”
occurrences.kjv: I sleep, but my heart waketh: it is the voice of my beloved that knocketh, saying, Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled: for my head is filled with dew, and my locks with the drops of the night.

occurrences.bsb: I rose up to open for my beloved. My hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with flowing myrrh on the handles of the bolt.
occurrences.kjv: I rose up to open to my beloved; and my hands dropped with myrrh, and my fingers with sweet smelling myrrh, upon the handles of the lock.

occurrences.bsb: I opened for my beloved, but he had turned and gone. My heart sank at his departure. I sought him but did not find him. I called, but he did not answer.
occurrences.kjv: I opened to my beloved; but my beloved had withdrawn himself, and was gone: my soul failed when he spake: I sought him, but I could not find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer.

occurrences.bsb: Let us go early to the vineyards to see if the vine has budded, if the blossom has opened, if the pomegranates are in bloom—there I will give you my love.
occurrences.kjv: Let us get up early to the vineyards; let us see if the vine flourish, whether the tender grape appear, and the pomegranates bud forth: there will I give thee my loves.

occurrences.bsb: None of them grows weary or stumbles; no one slumbers or sleeps. No belt is loose and no sandal strap is broken.
occurrences.kjv: None shall be weary nor stumble among them; none shall slumber nor sleep; neither shall the girdle of their loins be loosed, nor the latchet of their shoes be broken:

occurrences.bsb: who turned the world into a desert and destroyed its cities, who refused to let the captives return to their homes?”
occurrences.kjv: That made the world as a wilderness, and destroyed the cities thereof; that opened not the house of his prisoners?

occurrences.bsb: the LORD had already spoken through Isaiah son of Amoz, saying, “Go, remove the sackcloth from your waist and the sandals from your feet.” And Isaiah did so, walking around naked and barefoot.
occurrences.kjv: At the same time spake the Lord by Isaiah the son of Amoz, saying, Go and loose the sackcloth from off thy loins, and put off thy shoe from thy foot. And he did so, walking naked and barefoot.

occurrences.bsb: I will place on his shoulder the key to the house of David. What he opens no one can shut, and what he shuts no one can open.
occurrences.kjv: And the key of the house of David will I lay upon his shoulder; so he shall open, and none shall shut; and he shall shut, and none shall open.

occurrences.bsb: Whoever flees the sound of panic will fall into the pit, and whoever climbs from the pit will be caught in the snare. For the windows of heaven are open, and the foundations of the earth are shaken.
occurrences.kjv: And it shall come to pass, that he who fleeth from the noise of the fear shall fall into the pit; and he that cometh up out of the midst of the pit shall be taken in the snare: for the windows from on high are open, and the foundations of the earth do shake.

occurrences.bsb: Open the gates so a righteous nation may enter—one that remains faithful.
occurrences.kjv: Open ye the gates, that the righteous nation which keepeth the truth may enter in.

occurrences.bsb: Does the plowman plow for planting every day? Does he continuously loosen and harrow the soil?
occurrences.kjv: Doth the plowman plow all day to sow? doth he open and break the clods of his ground?

occurrences.bsb: Then the eyes of the blind will be opened and the ears of the deaf unstopped.
occurrences.kjv: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.

occurrences.bsb: I will open rivers on the barren heights, and fountains in the middle of the valleys. I will turn the desert into a pool of water, and the dry land into flowing springs.
occurrences.kjv: I will open rivers in high places, and fountains in the midst of the valleys: I will make the wilderness a pool of water, and the dry land springs of water.

occurrences.bsb: This is what the LORD says to Cyrus His anointed, whose right hand I have grasped to subdue nations before him, to disarm kings, to open the doors before him, so that the gates will not be shut:
occurrences.kjv: Thus saith the Lord to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have holden, to subdue nations before him; and I will loose the loins of kings, to open before him the two leaved gates; and the gates shall not be shut;

occurrences.bsb: Drip down, O heavens, from above, and let the skies pour down righteousness. Let the earth open up that salvation may sprout and righteousness spring up with it; I, the LORD, have created it.
occurrences.kjv: Drop down, ye heavens, from above, and let the skies pour down righteousness: let the earth open, and let them bring forth salvation, and let righteousness spring up together; I the Lord have created it.

occurrences.bsb: You have never heard; you have never understood; for a long time your ears have not been open. For I knew how deceitful you are; you have been called a rebel from birth.
occurrences.kjv: Yea, thou heardest not; yea, thou knewest not; yea, from that time that thine ear was not opened: for I knew that thou wouldest deal very treacherously, and wast called a transgressor from the womb.

occurrences.bsb: The Lord GOD has opened My ears, and I have not been rebellious, nor have I turned back.
occurrences.kjv: The Lord God hath opened mine ear, and I was not rebellious, neither turned away back.

occurrences.bsb: The captive will soon be freed; he will not die in the dungeon, and his bread will not be lacking.
occurrences.kjv: The captive exile hasteneth that he may be loosed, and that he should not die in the pit, nor that his bread should fail.

occurrences.bsb: Shake off your dust! Rise up and sit on your throne, O Jerusalem. Remove the chains from your neck, O captive Daughter of Zion.
occurrences.kjv: Shake thyself from the dust; arise, and sit down, O Jerusalem: loose thyself from the bands of thy neck, O captive daughter of Zion.

occurrences.bsb: He was oppressed and afflicted, yet He did not open His mouth. He was led like a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is silent, so He did not open His mouth.
occurrences.kjv: He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he opened not his mouth: he is brought as a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is dumb, so he openeth not his mouth.

occurrences.bsb: Isn’t this the fast that I have chosen: to break the chains of wickedness, to untie the cords of the yoke, to set the oppressed free and tear off every yoke?
occurrences.kjv: Is not this the fast that I have chosen? to loose the bands of wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens, and to let the oppressed go free, and that ye break every yoke?

occurrences.bsb: Your gates will always stand open; they will never be shut, day or night, so that the wealth of the nations may be brought into you, with their kings being led in procession.
occurrences.kjv: Therefore thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night; that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles, and that their kings may be brought.

occurrences.bsb: Then the LORD said to me, “Disaster from the north will be poured out on all who live in the land.
occurrences.kjv: Then the Lord said unto me, Out of the north an evil shall break forth upon all the inhabitants of the land.

occurrences.bsb: Their quivers are like open graves; they are all mighty men.
occurrences.kjv: Their quiver is as an open sepulchre, they are all mighty men.

occurrences.bsb: The cities of the Negev have been shut tight, and no one can open them. All Judah has been carried into exile, wholly taken captive.
occurrences.kjv: The cities of the south shall be shut up, and none shall open them: Judah shall be carried away captive all of it, it shall be wholly carried away captive.

occurrences.bsb: But now, behold, I am freeing you today from the chains that were on your wrists. If it pleases you to come with me to Babylon, then come, and I will take care of you. But if it seems wrong to you to come with me to Babylon, go no farther. Look, the whole land is before you. Wherever it seems good and right to you, go there.”
occurrences.kjv: And now, behold, I loose thee this day from the chains which were upon thine hand. If it seem good unto thee to come with me into Babylon, come; and I will look well unto thee: but if it seem ill unto thee to come with me into Babylon, forbear: behold, all the land is before thee: whither it seemeth good and convenient for thee to go, thither go.

occurrences.bsb: The LORD has opened His armory and brought out His weapons of wrath, for this is the work of the Lord GOD of Hosts in the land of the Chaldeans.
occurrences.kjv: The Lord hath opened his armoury, and hath brought forth the weapons of his indignation: for this is the work of the Lord God of hosts in the land of the Chaldeans.

occurrences.bsb: Come against her from the farthest border. Break open her granaries; pile her up like mounds of grain. Devote her to destruction; leave her no survivors.
occurrences.kjv: Come against her from the utmost border, open her storehouses: cast her up as heaps, and destroy her utterly: let nothing of her be left.

occurrences.bsb: In the thirtieth year, on the fifth day of the fourth month, while I was among the exiles by the River Kebar, the heavens opened and I saw visions of God.
occurrences.kjv: Now it came to pass in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, in the fifth day of the month, as I was among the captives by the river of Chebar, that the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God.

occurrences.bsb: So I opened my mouth, and He fed me the scroll.
occurrences.kjv: So I opened my mouth, and he caused me to eat that roll.

occurrences.bsb: But when I speak with you, I will open your mouth, and you are to tell them, ‘This is what the Lord GOD says.’ Whoever listens, let him listen; and whoever refuses, let him refuse, for they are a rebellious house.
occurrences.kjv: But when I speak with thee, I will open thy mouth, and thou shalt say unto them, Thus saith the Lord God; He that heareth, let him hear; and he that forbeareth, let him forbear: for they are a rebellious house.

occurrences.bsb: In his right hand appears the portent for Jerusalem, where he is to set up battering rams, to call for the slaughter, to lift a battle cry, to direct the battering rams against the gates, to build a ramp, and to erect a siege wall.
occurrences.kjv: At his right hand was the divination for Jerusalem, to appoint captains, to open the mouth in the slaughter, to lift up the voice with shouting, to appoint battering rams against the gates, to cast a mount, and to build a fort.

occurrences.bsb: Now prophesy, son of man, and declare that this is what the Lord GOD says concerning the Ammonites and their contempt: ‘A sword! A sword is drawn for slaughter, polished to consume, to flash like lightning—
occurrences.kjv: And thou, son of man, prophesy and say, Thus saith the Lord God concerning the Ammonites, and concerning their reproach; even say thou, The sword, the sword is drawn: for the slaughter it is furbished, to consume because of the glittering:

occurrences.bsb: On that day your mouth will be opened to him who has escaped; you will speak and no longer be mute. So you will be a sign to them, and they will know that I am the LORD.”
occurrences.kjv: In that day shall thy mouth be opened to him which is escaped, and thou shalt speak, and be no more dumb: and thou shalt be a sign unto them; and they shall know that I am the Lord.

occurrences.bsb: therefore I will indeed expose the flank of Moab beginning with its frontier cities—Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon, and Kiriathaim—the glory of the land.
occurrences.kjv: Therefore, behold, I will open the side of Moab from the cities, from his cities which are on his frontiers, the glory of the country, Beth–jeshimoth, Baal–meon, and Kiriathaim,

occurrences.bsb: Now the evening before the fugitive arrived, the hand of the LORD was upon me, and He opened my mouth before the man came to me in the morning. So my mouth was opened and I was no longer mute.
occurrences.kjv: Now the hand of the Lord was upon me in the evening, afore he that was escaped came; and had opened my mouth, until he came to me in the morning; and my mouth was opened, and I was no more dumb.

occurrences.bsb: Therefore prophesy and tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘O My people, I will open your graves and bring you up from them, and I will bring you back to the land of Israel.
occurrences.kjv: Therefore prophesy and say unto them, Thus saith the Lord God; Behold, O my people, I will open your graves, and cause you to come up out of your graves, and bring you into the land of Israel.

occurrences.bsb: Then you, My people, will know that I am the LORD, when I open your graves and bring you up from them.
occurrences.kjv: And ye shall know that I am the Lord, when I have opened your graves, O my people, and brought you up out of your graves,

occurrences.bsb: And the LORD said to me, “This gate is to remain shut. It shall not be opened, and no man shall enter through it, because the LORD, the God of Israel, has entered through it. Therefore it will remain shut.
occurrences.kjv: Then said the Lord unto me; This gate shall be shut, it shall not be opened, and no man shall enter in by it; because the Lord, the God of Israel, hath entered in by it, therefore it shall be shut.

occurrences.bsb: “This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘The gate of the inner court that faces east must be kept shut during the six days of work, but on the Sabbath day and on the day of the New Moon it shall be opened.
occurrences.kjv: Thus saith the Lord God; The gate of the inner court that looketh toward the east shall be shut the six working days; but on the sabbath it shall be opened, and in the day of the new moon it shall be opened.

occurrences.bsb: When the prince makes a freewill offering to the LORD, whether a burnt offering or a peace offering, the gate facing east must be opened for him. He is to offer his burnt offering or peace offering just as he does on the Sabbath day. Then he shall go out, and the gate must be closed after he goes out.
occurrences.kjv: Now when the prince shall prepare a voluntary burnt offering or peace offerings voluntarily unto the Lord, one shall then open him the gate that looketh toward the east, and he shall prepare his burnt offering and his peace offerings, as he did on the sabbath day: then he shall go forth; and after his going forth one shall shut the gate.

occurrences.bsb: And suddenly one with the likeness of a man touched my lips, and I opened my mouth and said to the one standing before me, “My lord, because of the vision, I am overcome with anguish, and I have no strength.
occurrences.kjv: And, behold, one like the similitude of the sons of men touched my lips: then I opened my mouth, and spake, and said unto him that stood before me, O my lord, by the vision my sorrows are turned upon me, and I have retained no strength.

occurrences.bsb: asking, “When will the New Moon be over, that we may sell grain? When will the Sabbath end, that we may market wheat? Let us reduce the ephah and increase the shekel; let us cheat with dishonest scales.
occurrences.kjv: Saying, When will the new moon be gone, that we may sell corn? and the sabbath, that we may set forth wheat, making the ephah small, and the shekel great, and falsifying the balances by deceit?

occurrences.bsb: The river gates are thrown open and the palace collapses.
occurrences.kjv: The gates of the rivers shall be opened, and the palace shall be dissolved.

occurrences.bsb: Look at your troops—they are like your women! The gates of your land are wide open to your enemies; fire consumes their bars.
occurrences.kjv: Behold, thy people in the midst of thee are women: the gates of thy land shall be set wide open unto thine enemies: the fire shall devour thy bars.

occurrences.bsb: See the stone I have set before Joshua; on that one stone are seven eyes. Behold, I will engrave on it an inscription, declares the LORD of Hosts, and I will remove the iniquity of this land in a single day.
occurrences.kjv: For behold the stone that I have laid before Joshua; upon one stone shall be seven eyes: behold, I will engrave the graving thereof, saith the Lord of hosts, and I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day.

occurrences.bsb: Open your doors, O Lebanon, that the fire may consume your cedars!
occurrences.kjv: Open thy doors, O Lebanon, that the fire may devour thy cedars.

occurrences.bsb: “On that day a fountain will be opened to the house of David and the people of Jerusalem, to cleanse them from sin and impurity.
occurrences.kjv: In that day there shall be a fountain opened to the house of David and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem for sin and for uncleanness.

occurrences.bsb: Bring the full tithe into the storehouse, so that there may be food in My house. Test Me in this,” says the LORD of Hosts. “See if I will not open the windows of heaven and pour out for you blessing without measure.
occurrences.kjv: Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse, that there may be meat in mine house, and prove me now herewith, saith the Lord of hosts, if I will not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing, that there shall not be room enough to receive it.
